projects.title: Solvefy
projects.meta: Featured case · Product design, AI, growth
projects.eyebrow: Featured case · Staff Product Designer / Product Design Lead · 2024–2026
projects.summary: A communications company two decades in the making, reborn as a technology ecosystem. I owned design and growth through the change.

blocks.text: Solvefy came from Ativos Capital, a company built over 20 years. I coordinated the rebrand that took 5 disconnected brands with inconsistent messaging and turned them into one integrated business ecosystem.

Research first. Stakeholder interviews and market analysis grounded the rebrand, and we defined the metrics we would track to prove it worked.

One ecosystem. Brand, communication tracks and social strategy unified across every sub brand, plus two live events.

A system, not just a logo. A design system shipped alongside the brand, orchestrating every product and touchpoint under one language.

Built for sales too. Sales playbooks and events gave the commercial team a clear path to sell the new ecosystem.
I reorganized how the product portfolio was structured across four products. NPS climbed, and navigation and campaign dispatch got noticeably smoother for every team using it.

Four products, one direction. Disparo Pro, Brasilfone, EasyCDP and Solvefy Cloud, working close to tech and operations.

End to end craft. Information architecture, wireframes, high fidelity prototypes and responsive systems built to scale, not one offs.

NPS climbed. Navigation and campaign dispatch got noticeably smoother for every team using the products daily.
I shipped AI driven design workflows while the company launched Agents, its AI orchestration product. Design that ships with AI, not around it.

AI in the process. Design workflows built and shipped on AI, run through Claude Code, MCPs and custom agents, shortening delivery cycles for the whole team.

AI in the product too. While I worked on this, Solvefy launched Agents, its own AI orchestration product for customers.

Not on the slide. The distinction that matters: AI as something I build with daily, not a line in a deck.

stats.label: shipped with AI, not around it

blocks.text: A clear OKR: find and qualify leads fast. I designed and built the platform that did it, end to end, in the sales team's hands.

Workspaces per ICP. Each product and each ideal customer got its own workspace, so no hunt bled into another.

Search with context. It matched companies by how they'd use what we sold, by CNAE across the Brazilian registry, pulled the decision-makers and C-levels from LinkedIn, and ranked every lead on one page by market score.

Ready to sell. Playbook, contact journey and the MQL/SQL split came built in, and a direct API pushed leads straight into Spotter, the tool the commercial team already used.

Beaten on day one. The month's target, 200 leads for product A and 100 for product B, fell on the first day of use.
I brought research into how we designed and shipped. Decisions grounded in real pain and churn data, not opinion.

Start with the pain. Research to find where the product actually hurt customers, not where we assumed it did.

Churn, then quick wins. Churn analysis turned into a short list of fixes that won people back.

PLG for the experience. Product-led-growth strategy set the direction for a better product and CX.

It held the revenue. The team I led shipped the research, blueprints and calls that lifted usability, and talked three large clients, roughly 18% of revenue, out of leaving.
I led a team of 7. We seeded a Winning by Design culture and stronger knowledge sharing, so design and growth pulled toward the same business outcomes.

Design and growth, aligned. A team of 7, pulling toward the same business outcomes instead of two separate agendas.

Winning by Design. Seeded as the team's operating culture, not a one off workshop.

Knowledge that travels. Stronger knowledge sharing so the team's work compounded instead of restarting every time.

projects.title: Remessa Online
projects.eyebrow: Case · Product Design Lead, Growth · Mar–Nov 2022 · Remote
projects.summary: Product Design Lead for Growth: a team of five and a mandate that reached past the logged in product — channels and acquisition, run shoulder to shoulder with marketing, and the website under my team.

blocks.text: Anyone who lands on a cross border payments site arrives with one question: how much do I actually receive? We were answering it eight times.

One question. Every visitor, sending or receiving, is really asking the same thing: what lands on the other side.

Eight answers. Eight currency simulators spread across the site and the funnel, each producing its own version of the truth.
Eight simulators, each sitting on a different stack. That is not an inconsistency problem — it is a paradigm problem, and you do not solve it by redesigning eight screens.

Modelled inside out. The product had been shaped around our internal technology boundaries instead of around the user's question.

Why redesign was the wrong tool. Restyling eight screens would have kept eight sources of truth. The model had to change, not the paint.
We took eight down to three. Not to one — and the reason is worth stating plainly: technology, not design. The stacks underneath could not be collapsed further.

Eight to three. Consolidated around the user's question, not around our org chart.

The limit, out loud. One was the right answer and three was the honest one: merging the remaining stacks meant a rebuild the business was not going to fund. Design stopped where technology drew the line, and we said so.

stats.label: the limit was technical, and named

blocks.text: The lasting part was not the count. It was agreeing, across design and marketing, how we speak to this audience and what each product should show in order to convert.

One voice. Design and marketing on the same definition of the audience, and the same language for money crossing a border.

One job per surface. What each product must show to convert, agreed and written down.

Why it holds. Without that alignment, simulators multiply again the moment a new channel needs one.

projects.title: Leads2b
projects.eyebrow: Case · Product Design Lead · Sales engagement
projects.summary: The structure that outlasted me. Sales engagement software redesigned around its real object — the cadence — and a structural division that still guides the product today, four years on.

blocks.text: Leads2b is sales engagement software. Its core object is not a screen — it is the cadence: the sequence of touches a salesperson builds, runs and reworks.

Home, flow, cadence. I redesigned the home, the flow, and the way a cadence gets built and rebuilt.

Designed for rework. A cadence is never finished — salespeople rebuild it constantly, so the building itself had to be the interface.

stats.label: the product's real object, not a screen

blocks.text: The structural division I made still guides the product today, four years on.
Verifiable from outside. Anyone can open Leads2b today and see the structure. There is no number to take on faith — the proof is the shipping product.

stats.label: the division still guides the product

blocks.text: A team of five, mixed content and design. In a tool salespeople speak through, the words are product, not decoration.

Content is product. A cadence is made of text — the messages are the mechanism, not the copy around it.

One craft, two materials. Leading writers and designers together was not an accumulation of roles. For this product it was the correct composition.
Churn stabilized while this settled in. I will not claim sole cause — the structure is the part I can still point at, four years later.

projects.title: Feel.U
projects.summary: Brand identity for Feel.U, a music label and artist collective focused on electronic music — danceable, introspective and experimental. The logotype is built from micro filaments that expand and contract with ambient sound, generating a different mark for every situation, alongside a Brand Maker platform that shapes forms from sound waves captured by the microphone.

blocks.text:
Feel.U
Branding/ Design/ Sound

⌅

–– Uma marca para cada beat.

Feel.U é um selo musical e coletivo de artistas focado em música eletrônica: dançante, introspectiva e experimental.

Imergindo nessa cultura e posicionamento, partimos para explorar possibilidades gráficas que pudessem criar uma identidade visual aberta e mutável, que preservasse a essência da marca, mas que pudesse traduzir a dinâmica e variedade que permeia o trabalho dos seus artistas. A partir desse conceito desenvolvemos uma marca composta por micro filamentos, que formam a tipografia do logotipo. Desses minúsculos pontos, linhas se expandem e contraem conforme o som do ambiente e criam uma marca diferente para cada situação específica. Para materializar o conceito construímos uma plataforma chamada Feel.U Brand Maker, que cria novas formas usando ondas sonoras capturadas pelo microfone do computador ou smartphone (apenas Android, #rip Apple que não autoriza a utilização de microfone no browser). Sem aleatoriedades, repetições ou padrões pré-definidos. Além disso, o Brand Maker será utilizado como projeção de parede nas festas e shows organizadas pela marca.

Coloque seu som, clique e salve a marca Feel.U da sua música preferida.
Cada artista, uma marca. Cada marca, um experimento.​​​​​​​

⇥ https://feelu.me​​​​​​​

projects.title: Mononoke · Progresso
projects.eyebrow: Album cover and music video · Mononoke · 2021
projects.summary: Cover art for Progresso by the crust/screamo punk band Mononoke, an album whose lyrics confront a society sold on unsustainable mechanical progress. The work spans the album cover, the single cover for Raymond, and a music video for the track, with text effects made analog by projecting onto fabric before being applied digitally.

blocks.text: /album_cover_art

Mononoke é uma banda punk de crust/screamo.

As letras nesse disco, chamado Progresso, falam sobre o lugar onde fomos jogados.

Sob o Sol de uma sociedade que tenta nos engana diariamente com discursos de um progresso mecânico insustentável, compreendemos que as inflamações decorrentes de choques fazem doer o tecido que assegura nossa existência como sociedade.

Nossas posições políticas nos trouxeram a imagem da guerreira que luta contra os abusos sofridos pela natureza como um símbolode resistência, por isso o nome trazido da linda animação do estúdio ecoativista Gibli .

As diferentes texturas e movimentos são o eterno desencaixe que sentimos. Como muitos brasileiros, somos diariamente confrontados com as adversidades e miséria de muitos. O projeto ainda em curso no Brasil tem como objetivo calar o pensar de todos aqueles que sofrem, fazer com que se sintam abençoados por terem o mínimo e pregar que todos temos direitos iguais e oportunidades.

_

Mononoke is a crust/screamo punk band.

The lyrics on this album, called Progresso, talk about the place where we were played.Under the sun of a society that tries to deceive us daily with speeches of unsustainable mechanical progress, we understand that inflammation resulting from shocks hurts the fabric that ensures our existence as a society.

Our political positions brought us the image of the warrior who fights against the abuses suffered by nature as a symbol of resistance, that's why the name was brought from the beautiful animation of the eco-activist studio Gibli.

The different textures and movements are the eternal detachment that we feel. Like many Brazilians, we are daily faced with the adversities and misery of many. The project still underway in Brazil aims to silence the thinking of all those who suffer, make them feel blessed for having the minimum and preach that we all have equal rights and opportunities.

In one of the last countries in the world to ban slavery, social and historical erasure is the rule.

/music_video
Mononoke - Raymond (2019)

Mersault, protagonista do livro O Estrangeiro, se deixa levar pela amizade com seu vizinho Raymond que o coloca numa situação que compromete sua vida.

Ele serve é uma metáfora social sobre como nos prendemos na cidade, com contratos, empregos e compromissos. Assim como Meursault, acabamos sendo levados indiferentemente para uma grande armadilha da civilização, ganhando pequenas comodidades para continuar fazer a máquina girar.

_

Raymond
(letra de Yuri Radziwill)

Na agressão chamada cidade
Às vezes crio péssimos laços
Que me mantém firmemente amarrado

Com distrações sonho acordado
Me afundo no poço chamado progresso
Que me mantém firmemente amarrado

Afundando em progresso

_

Mersault, protagonist of the book The Foreigner, lets himself be carried away by the friendship with his neighbor Raymond who puts him in a situation that compromises his life.

It serves as a social metaphor for how we lock ourselves in the city, with contracts, jobs and commitments. Like Meursault, we ended up being indifferently taken to a great trap of civilization, gaining small amenities to continue to spin the machine.

_

Raymond
(lyrics by Yuri Radziwill)

In the aggression called city
Sometimes I create lousy bonds
that keeps me firmly tied

With waking dream distractions
I sink into the well called progressthat keeps me firmly tied
Sinking in progress

Os efeitos no texto foram feitos de forma analógica com projeção em tecido e aplicação digital posterior.

_

The effects on the text were done in an analog way with projection on fabric and later digital application.
/raymond_single_cover

blocks.alt: Image may contain: cartoon, illustration and art

blocks.text:
O que é progresso? Está muito longe do que o neoliberalismo coloca à partir de uma visão de produção e opressão de vidas que perambulam tentando sanar suas dívidas e medos, suas depressões e cansaços causados por toda a pressão de sermos mais à todo momento, em tudo.

Vemos o progresso de forma tecnocrática, dataísta, onde esquece-se que números são desprovidos de narrativa, são duros e impessoais, servem para tudo, hoje, até para mostrar o quanto os outros são mais interessantes, ativando assim a visão de nós mesmos como projetos.

Coisificamos a nós mesmos para que não nos sentíssemos menos.
Nos fechamos dentro de nossas fortalezas de concreto e aço.
Acabamos aos poucos com o espaço comum e de troca.

_

What is progress? It is far from what neoliberalism puts on the basis of a vision of production and oppression of lives that roam around trying to remedy their debts and fears, their depressions and fatigue caused by all the pressure to be more all the time, in everything.

We see progress in a technocratic, dataistic way, where we forget that numbers are devoid of narrative, they are hard and impersonal, they serve everything today, even to show how much more others are more interesting, thus activating the view of ourselves as projects.

We objectify ourselves so that we don't feel less.
We shut ourselves up inside our concrete and steel fortresses.
We gradually ended up with the common and exchange space.
